A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Memory-Augmented Potential Field Theory and MA-MPPI research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable. V2 retains Appendices A–K but removes v1's NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original robotic-control, UAV, and power-system simulation results, including baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity tests, and generalization experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, replaces the robotic reward results in Table 1, and adds brief pilot findings.

M1.justification: The specified memory representation, feature detection, memory updates, potential construction, and MPPI control equations are unchanged. Covariance scaling already appears in v1's Appendix G.4. V2's calibration details and constrained/smoothed-controller pilot descriptions do not specify a new algorithmic step or component.

E1.justification: The four robotic benchmarks, UAV scenarios, and IEEE 39-bus system are retained; the latter was already specified in v1's Appendix I.4. V2 mentions repetitive-task and dynamic-environment pilots without identifying their settings sufficiently to establish whether they extend coverage beyond the existing experiments.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–4 and Appendices H/I remain unchanged. LOG-MPPI and DRPA-MPPI are newly discussed, not reported as evaluated baselines. The constrained/smoothed-MPPI pilot improvements lack explicit reference comparators, leaving their effect on comparator membership uncertain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces AUC-2000 and Final-2000, defined using the final 200 steps, in place of the main text's emphasis on asymptotic sample efficiency. It also explicitly caps RL interactions at the already stated 2000-step run length. These reported evaluation revisions are not reconciled with retained asymptotic descriptions. Appendix I.1 changes Motion Transformer's stated optimizer from AdamW to Adam; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds brief pilots testing compatibility with constrained and smoothed MPPI, reports unchanged rankings under ±25% cost-weight variation, and mentions a dynamic-environment pilot. Existing component ablations, trap analyses, hyperparameter sensitivity tables, and Appendix K generalization experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 independent runs with different seeds, standard deviations, and paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction at p < 0.01. Changed Table 1 means and deviations do not change the uncertainty-reporting practice. The removed checklist largely repeats these retained disclosures.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces every method's rewards across all four benchmarks. For Humanoid, MA-MPPI changes from 5239.1±290.5 to 4978.5±283.1, and SAC from 4125.3±276.2 to 936.7±354.9. These are revised results under changed evaluation framing, not established same-setting performance changes. V2 also adds approximately 15% success and 23% escape-time pilot improvements. Tables 2–15 retain their results.

T1.justification: V2 newly supplies a mathematical definition of the shared experimental objective and obstacle potential in Equation 17. This is a limited formalization addition: the stochastic-control framework, Theorems 3.1–3.3, their assumptions, and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows convergence language from guarantees of reaching global optima to reaching a neighborhood with high probability under stated assumptions. It also qualifies the contribution by fixed-budget online control. The abstract and central memory-augmentation contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly states the full-state-feedback assumption and identifies state-estimation uncertainty and rapidly changing traps as unresolved boundaries, including the need for faster decay and change-point detection. V2 also interprets memory augmentation as compatible with constrained/smoothed MPPI. Existing generalization limitations remain in Appendix K.

D1.justification: V2 adds warm-up percentile guidance for detection thresholds, explicit cost terms, a collision penalty of 1000, and cost-weight selection instructions. It changes the advertised code location from an anonymous repository to GitHub and revises the reported Motion Transformer optimizer. Most appendix implementation details and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds LOG-MPPI, DRPA-MPPI, covariance-design, annealing, constrained-control, and smoothing research, positioning persistent memory as complementary. Some underlying references are replaced, including the power-system and Koopman sources. DDPG now cites a stochastic-value-gradients paper despite retaining its name and configuration; bibliography updates alone do not establish a changed baseline.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized additions and rewrites in the introduction, related work, evaluation, and limitations. It updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and removes the administrative NeurIPS checklist. The principal section sequence and technical appendices remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All seven figure images and fifteen table structures are retained. Figure 5 moves to page 7, Figure 7 to page 10, and Table 1 to page 8, with accompanying text reflow. Some relocated figure/prose blocks interrupt sentences. Table 1's numerical replacements are result changes, not a table redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 improves qualifications, related-work coverage, and implementation disclosure, but weakens the consistency of the principal empirical comparison. The retained 27% Humanoid advantage matches v1's Table 1 but not v2's 4978.5 versus 936.7. Newly promised AUC-2000, Final-2000, and learning curves are not clearly presented, while asymptotic descriptions persist. The added pilots lack explicit comparison settings. These problems modestly outweigh the documentation gains by making the revised experimental evidence harder to interpret.
